SourceString: Adds to your damage and multiplies it — paw and aura alike. Two brackets in one node: the flat bonus sums with itself, the multiplier rides on top.
Adds to every kitten's damage. Scales with how many kittens you own, so it pairs with Vitality.
More kittens, permanently. They hunt on their own and keep earning while you aim elsewhere.
Gives you the AURA: everything inside your reach takes continuous damage, instead of one mouse at a time. Its Aura Radius shop line appears once you own it.
Makes the aura hurt more. Needs the Aura.
Permanently widens the aura. The shop line does the same thing for one run; this one keeps it.
Teaches you to POUNCE — a burst on {pounce}, worth more if you time it into a vulnerable window. Its two shop lines appear once you own it.
Makes each Pounce hit harder. Needs Pounce.
Pounce fires itself the moment it is ready, and you earn more while the game is shut. The auto-fired burst is worth less than one you timed yourself — that is the trade.
Damage past a mouse's last hit point splashes onto the nearest survivor instead of evaporating.
Raises the share that splashes. Needs Overkill.
The cat rides a unicorn now, as is its right. Opens everything the Unicorn can be made to do.
Unlocks Rainbow Poop. It is exactly as unpleasant as it sounds and it kills things.
Multiplies Rainbow Poop's damage. Needs Rainbow Poop.
Every mouse is worth more Catnip, and Golden Mice turn up more often. It does not make you kill faster — it makes the killing pay.
Everything on the ground moves like it is wading. Not just inside your reach — the whole floor is yours. Fliers do not care.
The wading gets worse. At the last rung a mouse on the ground barely moves at all.
A mouse about to wander off the edge is turned back instead. Roughly a third of everything that spawns currently leaves without paying you.
A mouse you finish off while it is already nearly dead pays more. Bat it around first.
The horn fires a continuous beam at whatever is nearest. It is a share of your AURA, so every point you have ever put into the aura is already in it.
When the beam kills something it jumps to the next thing. And the next.
Anything the beam finishes off pays more. The only thing in the game that makes you want a mouse to stay alive one more second.
The beam stops picking targets and simply sweeps, hitting everything it crosses.
Beam kills leave shards. Enough shards and the whole screen goes off at once.
The next run starts further along: you keep a share of your Catnip, your shop lines start already levelled, and you open in a deeper biome. Only ever as deep as you have already earned.
All shoulder and no reach. What you can touch is flattened; the aura shrinks to half.
Commits absolutely. Pounce lands four times over, then you stand still for three seconds.
Heard for streets around. A far wider aura that hits for a good deal less.
Works alone. The aura more than doubles and the kittens stop dealing damage entirely.
Turns up with a clipboard. One more card in every hand, and every card taken arrives a level higher, for a fifth of your damage.
Declined every position. Ten percent more of everything, and it costs nothing at all.
Takes what is not nailed down. Far more Catnip from everything, and you hit a good deal softer for it.
Strikes rarely and enormously. Three times the crit chance, crits two and a half times as hard, and swung at half the speed.
Everything is owed to you. Two and a half times the Catnip, and the kittens barely scratch.
Calls them in. Twice as many arrive, and every one of them is half again as hard to put down.
Every hit leaves a dent, and dents stack. Doubles the ceiling the shop's own Shred line stops at.
You are still here. Every run starts with rerolls in hand - the one part of the card economy no shop line sells.
They owe you for every life you have already given them. Damage rises with every Reawaken on the save.
The floor is the weapon. Anything wading through your Snare takes far more from everything you have.
Catnip you have not spent works for you. A share of the bank is paid back every time the wave turns over.
The Cone of Shame is a countdown, not a sentence. Every kill you make while rooted cuts it short.
Hold still and the sound carries. Your reach grows the longer you stay put, and resets the moment you move.
Look over there. Ground mice wander toward you instead of away - the crowd the Magician gave up its kittens to gather.
Every job needs a buyer. Catnip climbs with each kill this wave and starts over when the wave turns.
The slower the swing, the worse it lands. Crit damage rises with everything that has made you slow.
Nothing leaves with its pockets full. Mice that wander off still pay you a share on the way out.
Stand around long enough and it adds up. The bank empties into your next kill.
Everyone pays eventually. Every hundredth kill settles up in a lump.
Word gets around. Every kill brings more of them, and the rush fades if you stop.
Nothing up your sleeve. Every so often one of them is simply not there any more - bosses excepted.
Some swings land twice. No warning, no wind-up - the second one is simply already there.
You do not land, you arrive. The ground you are rooted to burns for as long as you are stuck on it.
The sound gets there a moment after you do. A second, weaker ring keeps working where you just were.
A crit asks a question. Whatever the paw touches next does not get to answer it.
You have seen the plans. Part of the next hand is already known while you choose from this one.
You find the beat and keep it. Every tenth swing crits without asking, and switching targets does not lose your place.
The aura stops humming and starts pulsing. Everything inside takes the beat.
You know before they do. The next thing worth worrying about is marked where it will arrive.
Catnip you leave alone quietly grows, on the clock rather than on the kill.
The tangle spreads upward. Fliers that stray over the snared get dragged down into it - the only thing in the game that reaches them from the ground.
The swing does not stop at the first one. Whatever is lined up behind it gets the same blow - the aura you gave up, as a line.
You play to the room. The fuller the aura, the harder everything in it is hit.
Nothing is wasted. Damage that spilled past a kill comes back as Catnip.
Crits stop being luck. The same chance is spent on a fixed cadence instead - no better on average, and never a cold streak again.
They come to you now. Mice arrive in a ring around the cat instead of walking in from the edges.
Read the small print. A Pounce that rooted you and killed nothing costs no cooldown at all.
The kittens come back, and they are not really there. They do no damage - they simply herd everything into your aura.
Nobody said one job. Wear a second, at half its effect, good and bad alike.
The bait was always a paperwork problem. Pay the boss's summons in Catnip and skip the grind entirely.
One card in every hand comes off the bench early, already a level ahead.
Word gets out. They arrive far faster than the neighbourhood alone would send them - and this keeps climbing after the shop's Spawn Rate has nothing left to sell.
You stop waiting for permission. The moment the next biome opens you are already in it - and you can still switch it off if you want to linger.
The boss is summoned the instant you can afford it. Never mid-fight, and never without the Bait in hand.
A card is taken for you rather than stopping the game to ask. The pick screen only appears when you want it to.
A full room is easier, not harder. Everything you do hits harder while forty or more of them are on the floor.
And an empty one is personal. With fewer than five left you hit vastly harder - which is the exact opposite of Swarm Logic, and there is a gap in the middle where neither helps.
Some kills are excessive. Overshoot a mouse by ten times its own health and the leftovers go off where it stood.
They start to know your name. Damage climbs with every wave you survive here, and travelling loses all of it.
You are keeping score. Every card taken this run makes you harder, and a Reawaken settles the account.
The number speaks for itself. Every ten thousand kills this cycle is another permanent notch until you Reawaken.
Somebody organised them. Kittens go where the mice are thickest instead of grabbing whatever is nearest.
You get another look. Every Catches level hands you rerolls to spend on the hands that follow.
The kittens have been watching. They inherit a share of your crit chance - the first thing in the game that makes them scale with the paw.
One more card in every hand, for good. More things to choose between, permanently - not more of any one thing.
Reawakening pays out twice. Once when you do it, and once more the next time you reach the Park - so the second half is a reason to go back out.
You have been reading ahead. The realm list says what a biome pays before you go there.
Bait stops being stranded. What you earned anywhere counts everywhere.
